source: ACIAR AH/2005/086 'Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual' (Windsor, Bush & Young), Best Practice Health and Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia -- hosted at mekonglivestock.wordpress.com (University of Sydney / GDAHP project site)
text: Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS) is a bacterial disease of cattle and buffalo, often spreading from affected animals and more common with close herding or at the start of the rainy season. Signs include sudden death (sometimes of many animals at once), fever, loss of appetite, nasal discharge, increased salivation, laboured breathing, and swelling in the neck/jaw area. Treatment: alert the VAHW immediately, isolate animals to stop spread, provide shelter, hand-feeding and water, and note that antibiotics may help only if given very early and correctly -- once clinical signs are advanced, treatment is often too late. Prevention: vaccinate every 6 months, ideally one month before the rainy season; avoid contact with sick animals; isolate during outbreaks and don't mix herds; and avoid trading or transporting cattle with unknown disease history during an outbreak.
